recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It preserves the later DeviceDefinition scope rewrite while restoring the FHIR-30503 packaging boundary that implementers need in current build-scoped source.
issue_request: FHIR-30503 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It requested a recursive DeviceDefinition.packaging backbone with identifier, type, count, distributor, UDI device identifier, and nested packaging; it also required scope text clarifying that custom repackaging is out of scope and packaging for kits belongs at the kit level, while root DeviceDefinition.quantity and root DeviceDefinition.distributor should not remain.
initial_application: Commit f662eb0f7a initially applied the issue by adding the recursive packaging backbone and a Scope and Usage sentence about kit-level packaging and custom repackaging. Later commits refined the packaging structure, including FHIR-32785, FHIR-54860, and FHIR-55260.
additional_context: DeviceDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition already has DeviceDefinition.packaging 0..*, DeviceDefinition.packaging.packaging as a contentReference back to DeviceDefinition.packaging, packaging.count as integer, packaging.distributor only under packaging, and no root DeviceDefinition.quantity or root DeviceDefinition.distributor. The missing narrative sentence was removed when commit 578361a900 applied broader FHIR-24936 scope wording, not by a packaging-specific reversal. FHIR-29727 was withdrawn as superseded by FHIR-30503, and FHIR-25036 is only background because FHIR-30503 explicitly limited distributor to packaging/logistics context.
reconciliation: Added a narrow Scope and Usage paragraph to source/devicedefinition/devicedefinition-introduction.xml restoring the FHIR-30503 packaging boundary. No structural DeviceDefinition XML changes were needed.
source_changes: source/devicedefinition/devicedefinition-introduction.xml: Added a Scope and Usage paragraph for DeviceDefinition.packaging, kit-level packaging, and custom repackaging scope.
